metadata.description: Semicolon-separated email addresses for flow error notifications.

manual.description: Power Pages trigger — only callable from your Power Pages site. Registered in Power Pages site settings as SMKB/Flow/CheckOTP.

email.description: Email address of the user submitting the OTP.

otp.description: 6-digit OTP code entered by the user.

contextId.description: [ADAPT]: rename or remove to match smkb_sol_CreateOtp.

Main_Flow.description: All main flow logic. Business errors (NOT_FOUND, WRONG_OTP, LOCKED — expected conditions) use Response + Terminate(Succeeded) inside this scope and do NOT reach Handle_Flow_Error. Only unexpected technical failures bubble up.

Validate_Input.description: Guard: reject missing/malformed input before touching any data. Returns 400 + Terminate(Succeeded) so Handle_Flow_Error does NOT run — invalid input is not a bug.

Respond_invalid_input.description: Return 400 for missing/malformed email or OTP that is not exactly 6 characters.

Terminate_after_invalid_input.description: Stop the flow cleanly — no error email, no 500.

IMPLEMENT_Get_OTP_Record.description: Retrieve the stored OTP record for this email. [IMPLEMENT]: (1) replace entityName with your OTP table plural logical name (e.g. smkb_sol_otprequests). (2) replace smkb_sol_email in $filter with your email field name. Returns at most 1 record.

If_OTP_Not_Found.description: No OTP record found for this email — user never sent a code, or it was already consumed. Return NOT_FOUND + Terminate(Succeeded).

If_Account_Locked.description: Account is locked after 5 failed attempts — refuse before even comparing the OTP. [IMPLEMENT]: replace 'smkb_sol_attempts' with your actual attempts field name in the OTP table.

IMPLEMENT_PLACEHOLDER.description:
[IMPLEMENT — BUSINESS LOGIC]: Replace this Compose action with your actual OTP validation actions.

What to build (run in this order inside Main_Flow after If_Account_Locked):
  1. Check expiry: compare stored expires_at to utcNow(). If expired → Respond_expired({ code: 'LOCKED' }) + Terminate(Succeeded).
  2. Compare OTPs: if stored otp_code != triggerBody()?['otp']:
       a. Increment attempts counter on the OTP record (UpdateRecord).
       b. Compute attemptsRemaining = 5 - new_attempts_value.
       c. Respond_wrong_otp({ code: 'WRONG_OTP', attemptsRemaining: N }) + Terminate(Succeeded).
  3. On match:
       a. Delete the OTP record (DeleteRecord) — one-time use; leaving it enables replay attacks.
       b. Retrieve the user record from your main user table.
       c. Expose the user record ID for IMPLEMENT_Create_Auth_Session below (e.g. via a Compose or variable).

Security notes:
  - Always delete the OTP row on success — replay attacks are trivially prevented this way.
  - Expiry check MUST run before the comparison; expired codes should NOT increment the attempts counter.
  - Comparing plaintext 6-digit codes is safe here because the 5-attempt lockout prevents enumeration.

Session cleanup (optional but recommended):
  - Before creating the new auth session, delete any previous session rows for this email:
    ListRecords(smkb_sol_sessions, $filter: smkb_sol_email eq '...') → Apply_to_each → DeleteRecord.
    This prevents accumulation of valid tokens for the same user.
  - A scheduled cleanup flow running daily to delete expired rows is also recommended.

CRITICAL — two error categories:

(A) BUSINESS ERRORS (WRONG_OTP, LOCKED, NOT_FOUND, EXPIRED — expected, do NOT send error email):
    Pattern: Response(4xx) → Terminate(runStatus: Succeeded)
    Terminate(Succeeded) ends the run cleanly. Handle_Flow_Error does NOT run.

(B) TECHNICAL ERRORS (Dataverse failure, null reference — unexpected bugs):
    Let them throw unhandled. The scope fails → Handle_Flow_Error runs → error email sent → 500 returned.

Compose_Generate_Auth_Token.description: Generate a random auth token. guid() produces a UUID-4 format string — cryptographically suitable as an opaque session token.

IMPLEMENT_Create_Auth_Session.description: Create a session record in the Dataverse sessions table. [IMPLEMENT]: (1) replace entityName with your session table plural name (e.g. smkb_sol_sessions). (2) replace smkb_sol_token/smkb_sol_email/smkb_sol_expires_at/smkb_sol_userid with your actual field schema names. (3) set item/smkb_sol_userid to the user record ID from IMPLEMENT_PLACEHOLDER.

parameters.item/[IMPLEMENT]:smkb_sol_userid: [IMPLEMENT]: user record ID from IMPLEMENT_PLACEHOLDER — e.g. @outputs('Get_user_record')?['body/smkb_sol_userid']

Respond_to_PowerPages.description: Return the authenticated user record and auth token to the Power Pages caller. [IMPLEMENT]: replace inviteeId/firstName/lastName body fields with your actual user record expressions.

Handle_Flow_Error.description: Error handler — runs ONLY on unexpected technical failures (unhandled exception in Main_Flow). Business errors (WRONG_OTP, LOCKED, NOT_FOUND) use Terminate(Succeeded) inside Main_Flow and never reach here.

Check_Error_Emails_Configured.description: Only send the error email if smkb_sol_FlowErrorEmails is configured. Skipping silently when the env var is empty avoids spurious SendEmailV2 failures that would add noise to every error handler run.

Send_error_notification.description: Send error alert to all addresses in smkb_sol_FlowErrorEmails (semicolon-separated String env var).

parameters.emailMessage/Body:
@concat('

The flow smkb_sol_CheckOtp failed unexpectedly in the ', parameters('ENVIRONMENT_NAME (smkb_sol_EnvironmentName)'), ' environment.

Triggered by: ', coalesce(triggerBody()?['email'], '(unknown)'), '

Run ID: ', workflow()['run']['name'], '

Open Power Automate → Cloud flows → smkb_sol_CheckOtp → Run history to investigate.

')

Respond_with_error.description: Always return a response so the Power Pages caller does not hang.
